newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN refugee body seeks funds for Angola.
newsitem.headline: UN refugee body seeks funds for Angola.

text.p: The United Nations' refugee agency UNHCR launched a worldwide appeal for $38.2 million on Friday to help more than 300,000 Angolan refugees in central and southern Africa go home.

UNHCR officials said the funds were essential to speed up repatriation of people who fled to neighbouring countries during the long Angolan civil war -- ended with a precarious U.N.-brokered peace accord in 1994.
"Angola is at the crossroads," said Nicolas Bwakira, UNHCR regional director for southern Africa, in a statement on the appeal issued from the agency's headquarters in Geneva.
"Now more than ever we need to put in place programmes that will not only set the momentum for the return of refugees but also enable them to begin a new life."

The repatriation effort will be aimed at some 200,000 Angolans in Zaire, 96,000 in Zambia, 12,000 in the Congo Republic and 1,000 in Namibia as well as another 15,000 distributed in several other countries.
During two decades of conflict in Angola, at least 600,000 people were killed and some three million were forced to flee their homes.

Since UNHCR began operations last June, the statement said, around 74,000 refugees had returned and many more wanted to go back. But poor funding last year had prevented any proper programming, the statement said.
And to start up its programmes this year, the agency had been forced to borrow $3 million from a voluntary fund normally reserved for emergencies.
The appeal covers costs for transport and logistics, household support for returnees, health and nutrition, emergency shelter, crop production and education as well as operational costs.

The Angolan effort is UNHCR's second major refugee return operation in southern Africa. It follows the repatriation during 1995 of 1.7 million people who had fled abroad during the long civil war in Mozambique, another former Portuguese colony.
